column3: The Hebrew literally calls Egypt a “house of slaves.”
The Hebrew separately names a carved image and any likeness, rather than combining them into “an idol in the form of anything.” It explicitly locates the waters under the earth.
The Hebrew says “serve them,” rather than only “worship them.”
The Hebrew says “to thousands,” without expressly adding “generations” or changing it to a singular thousand.
The Hebrew says the people “saw” even the sounds and repeats their seeing; it names flames rather than explicitly lightning.
The Hebrew retains the image of His fear “before your faces.”
The Hebrew names a sword or cutting tool, rather than specifically a chisel, and describes lifting it over the altar.
